newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia rejects McDonnell trainer bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia rejects McDonnell trainer bid.

text.p: Australia on Friday rejected a bid by McDonnell Douglas Corp to supply its T-45 Goshawk aircraft for an air force trainer programme but retained bids by British Aerospace Plc and Aermacchi SpA.

"The Minister for Defence, Mr Ian McLachlan, today announced that Aermacchi of Italy with its Macchi MB.339FD and British Aerospace of the United Kingdom with the Hawk aircraft remain in the competition for the Royal Australian Air Force's new Lead-In Fighter," McLachlan's office said in a statement.

"The tender from McDonnell Douglas Aerospace of the United States has been eliminated on the basis that it is clearly less preferred in a number of key areas," the statement said, without elaborating.
The air force has called for tenders for up to 40 aircraft, leaving bidders to work out the exact number needed to fulfill its training requirement when its old Macchi MB.326s are retired in 2000.
The McDonnell Douglas aircraft is the U.S. Navy's verson of the British Aerospace Hawk, which remains in the competition.
However, McDonnell Douglas had offered AlliedSignal's new F124 turbofan engine in the T-45 as an alternative to the standard Rolls-Royce Adour, which is the only option in the Hawk.
Aermacchi's MB.339 uses the Rolls-Royce Viper tubojet.
McLachlan' statement said the preferred aircraft supplier was expected to be selected in late 1996.
"It is anticipated that Australian industry will play a major role in the assembly, test and ongoing support of the new aircraft."
The British Aerospace bid includes Qantas Airways Ltd, which would assemble, test, maintain and repair the trainers' engines.
